## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one

+/// The floating phone dock's occupied bottom height, for scroll views that
+/// run underneath it.
+///
+/// The narrow shell scaffold sets `extendBody` while the dock rides in its
+/// `bottomNavigationBar` slot, so the ambient [MediaQuery] padding.bottom
+/// inside the narrow body is INFLATED to exactly the dock's occupied height
+/// (home indicator + 8pt separation gap + 56pt pill). Sections consume that
+/// value as scroll padding so their final rows stay reachable above the
+/// glass instead of being cut behind the pill.
+///
+/// Desktop layouts never build the narrow scaffold: their raw inset stays
+/// 0 (and the desktop Duo camera profile seeds at most 34), which never
+/// reaches [minInflatedBottom] — so [bottomOf] resolves to 0 there and
+/// every caller keeps its legacy padding, keeping desktop geometry
+/// byte-identical.
+final class MessengerFloatingDockInsets {
+  MessengerFloatingDockInsets._();
+
+  /// 56pt pill ([MessengerBottomNavigation.height]) + 8pt bottom gap
+  /// ([MessengerBottomNavigation.bottomGap]) — the smallest inflated value
+  /// the narrow scaffold can report. Raw device safe areas (iOS home
+  /// indicator ≈ 34) stay below it, so only the scaffold's inflated inset
+  /// qualifies. (Literal: importing the controls file here would create an
+  /// import cycle.)
+  static const double minInflatedBottom = 64;
+
+  /// The dock's occupied bottom height, or 0 when the ambient MediaQuery
+  /// was not inflated for the floating dock (desktop, standalone hosts).
+  static double bottomOf(BuildContext context) {
+    final bottom = MediaQuery.paddingOf(context).bottom;
+    return bottom >= minInflatedBottom ? bottom : 0;
+  }
+}

# extendBody property

final

If true, and [bottomNavigationBar](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/bottomNavigationBar.html) or [persistentFooterButtons](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/persistentFooterButtons.html) is specified, then the [body](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/body.html) extends to the bottom of the Scaffold, instead of only extending to the top of the [bottomNavigationBar](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/bottomNavigationBar.html) or the [persistentFooterButtons](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/persistentFooterButtons.html).

If true, a [MediaQuery](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/widgets/MediaQuery-class.html) widget whose bottom padding matches the height of the [bottomNavigationBar](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/bottomNavigationBar.html) will be added above the scaffold's [body](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/body.html).

This property is often useful when the [bottomNavigationBar](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/bottomNavigationBar.html) has a non-rectangular shape, like [CircularNotchedRectangle](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/painting/CircularNotchedRectangle-class.html), which adds a [FloatingActionButton](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/FloatingActionButton-class.html) sized notch to the top edge of the bar. In this case specifying `extendBody: true` ensures that scaffold's body will be visible through the bottom navigation bar's notch.

See also:

- [extendBodyBehindAppBar](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/material/Scaffold/extendBodyBehindAppBar.html), which extends the height of the body to the top of the scaffold.

content.thinking:
The panel app bar is a `PreferredSize` of height `titlebarTop + kToolbarHeight` with the inner `AppBar(primary: false)`. Previously, the Scaffold (primary: true default) added `MediaQuery.padding.top` ON TOP of the preferredSize for the app bar slot → the canvasTopInset formula mirrored that (titlebarTop + kToolbarHeight + padding.top). The fix: `primary: false` on the Scaffold → slot height = preferredSize exactly → canvasTopInset = titlebarTop + kToolbarHeight. Consistent. The inner AppBar already has `primary: false` (pre-existing) so it doesn't double-pad either. The change is internally consistent, and the golden asserts canvas at 107 = 51+56. Good.

Edge: with `primary: false`, the Scaffold ALSO stops consuming the safe area for the appBar — extendBodyBehindAppBar: true puts the body behind the appBar; the canvas Padding(top: 107) handles it. On iOS, the status bar overlays the titlebarTop region — the panel chrome's glass underlay paints behind the status bar. That's the intended design.

Also `_appCanvas`: `fullChrome && panelChrome == null ? SafeArea(bottom: false, ...) : SafeArea(top: false, ...)` — for the panel chrome case SafeArea(top:false) — with the route's MediaQuery padding.top = 59, SafeArea(top:false) preserves bottom... fine, canvas content isn't inset at top by SafeArea (the Padding handles it). OK.

```dart
final fold = Platform.isLinux
    ? (String s) => s
    : (String s) => s.toLowerCase();
```

On Flutter web, `dart:io` `Platform` members throw `UnsupportedError: Platform._operatingSystem` at runtime. This file is web-compiled today (it already imports `dart:io`, and `flutter build web` is green on main), which is exactly why the same file guards its own Platform read at `project_mount_flow.dart:206`:

```dart
if (kIsWeb) return false;
return Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS;
```

(`chat_screen.dart:587` guards `Platform.isMacOS` the same way.)

**Reachable crash path (web is a shipped target — `ci.yml` `flutter build web`, `pages.yml` deploys it):**

- `chat_screen.dart:473` — `FilesAppPanel(initialPath: visibleFolderRoot(service.env, service.currentSessionCwd), ...)` — built with no `kIsWeb` gate whenever the Files panel opens.
- `visibleFolderRoot` → `_isSameFolderPath(visible, candidate)` → non-exact pair → `Platform.isLinux` → throw during build.

Pre-PR, a non-matching candidate returned `null` (gate shows / env cwd listing) — graceful. Post-PR, a restored or cross-device session whose recorded cwd differs from the live browser fs cwd crashes the Files panel build. The relocated-container scenario this PR fixes for iOS is precisely the "recorded cwd ≠ live root" shape that now throws on web.

**Suggested fix** (keep the exact-equality contract, degrade the fold on web):

```dart
final fold = (kIsWeb || Platform.isLinux)
    ? (String s) => s
    : (String s) => s.toLowerCase();
```

Web folds identity — exact matches still return early, and tail matches still fire when the case agrees; no iOS behavior changes. A unit test with a fake `kIsWeb` (the pattern `AgentService` tests already use, `main.dart:1084`) pins the web path.

🚨 **BLOCKING: Settings dock reserve reads the wrong context — Bug 1's settings leg is a silent no-op on the phone**

The narrow shell's settings arm calls `_buildSettingsPanel()` from `_narrowSectionSurface` → `_buildNarrowBody` while building the **Scaffold itself** — so the `context` here is `_WideLayoutShellState.context`, which sits **above** the shell Scaffold:

```dart
final dockReserve = _isNarrow
    ? MessengerFloatingDockInsets.bottomOf(context)   // State.context — above the Scaffold
    : 0.0;
```

But the inflated inset `bottomOf` is designed to read only exists **inside the Scaffold body**: with `extendBody: true`, Flutter adds "a MediaQuery widget whose bottom padding matches the height of the bottomNavigationBar **above the scaffold's body**" (Scaffold.extendBody docs, api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Scaffold/extendBody.html). The state's context is an ancestor of the Scaffold, so it reads the **raw** view padding — on an iPhone that is the 34pt home indicator, which fails the `>= minInflatedBottom (64)` gate and returns **0**.

Result on the phone: `SettingsCategoryPanel(bottomReserve: 0)` → the category list keeps its legacy 16pt bottom inset and its tail rows stay cut behind the 98pt floating dock — the exact Bug 1 surface the ticket names ("chats/activity/local/networks/settings") and the PR summary claims is reserved. Every other surface works because they call `bottomOf(context)` inside their own `build` (below the Scaffold): `_ChatListPanelState`, `_LocalSessionsPanelState`, `_ChatNetworksPanelState`, `_ActivityList`, `_ActivityDetail`. Settings is the one call site above the inflation. The new goldens pin chats/activity/keyboard only — settings has no golden, consistent with this leg being inert.

**Suggested fix** — mirror the other panels: pass `compact` (or the reserve) into `SettingsCategoryPanel` and resolve `MessengerFloatingDockInsets.bottomOf(context)` inside its `build`, where the context is below the shell Scaffold and sees the inflated 98pt:

```dart
// settings_navigation.dart — build()
final list = ListView(
  padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(8, topPadding + 4, 8,
      16 + (compact ? MessengerFloatingDockInsets.bottomOf(context) : 0)),
```

and keep `_buildSettingsPanel` passing `compact: _isNarrow`. Desktop stays at 0 (the shell never builds the narrow scaffold there), preserving byte-identical desktop goldens. Then add the missing narrow-settings golden to `narrow_layout_shell_ios_bottom_golden_test.dart` so the leg is pinned like chats/activity.

**Summary**: Two blocking findings in an otherwise well-evidenced batch: an unguarded `Platform.isLinux` in `_isSameFolderPath` crashes the Files panel on the shipped web build, and the Settings dock reserve reads the shell-state context above the Scaffold so the ≥64pt gate sees the raw 34pt home-indicator inset and the fix is a silent no-op on the phone. - 💡 Digest (below) — minor items, no threads.

All checks pass. Review complete — delivering the findings.

## Review Summary — PR #2112 (iOS layout batch)

**Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** — 2 🚨 BLOCKING findings, both with verified evidence chains; the other four iOS fixes (keyboard context, app-view/trajectory double-insets, relocated-sandbox listing, `_envPath` mount segment) check out against their goldens and unit tests, and desktop behavior is properly gated.

**🚨 1 — Web crash (`project_mount_flow.dart:121`)**: `_isSameFolderPath` evaluates `Platform.isLinux` eagerly on every non-exact path pair. On Flutter web, dart:io `Platform` throws `UnsupportedError` at runtime; the file is web-compiled today and `visibleFolderRoot` is called un-gated when the Files panel opens (`chat_screen.dart:473`). Any session whose recorded cwd differs from the live root — the same relocated-container shape the PR fixes for iOS — now crashes instead of gracefully gating. The file's own `kIsWeb` guard at line 206 proves the convention.

**🚨 2 — Settings dock fix is a no-op (`wide_layout_shell_settings.dart:15`)**: `bottomOf(State.context)` is read from the shell state's context **above** the narrow Scaffold. Per the Flutter `Scaffold.extendBody` docs, the inflated MediaQuery (98pt dock height) is injected **above the body** — the state context sees the raw 34pt home-indicator inset, fails the `>= 64` gate, and `bottomReserve` is always 0 on iPhone. Bug 1's settings leg (explicitly named in the ticket) stays broken; every other surface reads `bottomOf` inside its own build below the Scaffold. No settings golden exists to pin it.

Plus a 4-item ranked digest (64pt literal duplication, `max(76,…)` base inconsistency, pointer-down dismissal firing on scroll-start, override-reset teardown style) — suggestion/nit level, no threads.

Artifacts: `outputs/pr_review.json`, `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md`.
